premises.text: The makeup industry charges a premium for color that technology can provide for free
premises.evidence_span: the makeup industry makes a whole lot of money on a whole lot of bullshit. And they do this by charging a huge premium on one thing that technology provides for free. And that one thing is color.

premises.text: Mass outlets cannot offer the same color selection as prestige stores due to supply chain limitations
premises.evidence_span: Walmart can't offer you all the colors that expensive prestige stores can, like Sephora. Why? Supply chain.

premises.text: Mink provides the selection of prestige and the convenience of mass by allowing users to print makeup at home
premises.evidence_span: it gives you the selection of prestige, and it combines it with the convenience of mass.

premises.text: Mink operates like an inkjet printer and requires no new software to use
premises.evidence_span: it's a proprietary piece of hardware, and it works just like an inkjet printer. You do not need any new software.

premises.text: The initial target market for Mink is girls aged 13 to 21 who are still experimenting with makeup
premises.evidence_span: My initial target market, they're girls, ages 13 to 21. They have not formed any habits yet, and they're still experimenting.

premises.text: Mink can print a variety of makeup products beyond eyeshadow, including lipsticks and foundations
premises.evidence_span: we're printing eyeshadow right now, but this is basically going to be able to print lipsticks, powders, creams, foundations, et cetera.

premises.text: Mink empowers users to define their own beauty rather than relying on corporations
premises.evidence_span: this is going to finally train our girls to understand that the definition of beauty is something that they should be able to control, not our corporations.

value.text: Users gain control over their beauty choices through customizable makeup printing
value.evidence_span: the definition of beauty is something that they should be able to control, not our corporations.

notes: No external knowledge or traction metrics included.
